name: Hierarchical 3D Gaussian Splatting (H-3DGS)
text:
# Hierarchical 3D Gaussian Splatting (H-3DGS)
Also called: H-3DGS, Hierarchical-3DGS
## Overview
Hierarchical 3D Gaussian Splatting (H-3DGS) is a method for large-scale 3D reconstruction that addresses the memory bottlenecks of standard [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) by training scene chunks independently and merging them into a global Level-of-Detail (LoD) hierarchy [S1, unofficial]. Unlike standard 3DGS, which requires storing all Gaussian primitives in VRAM, H-3DGS uses chunking to mitigate memory usage during training, though this approach introduces specific boundary artifacts such as chunk bleeding and ghosting [S1, unofficial]. It builds on [3D Gaussian Splatting LOD methods](5439-3d-gaussian-splatting-lod-methods.md) by introducing a Split Point Tree (SPT) structure to manage the hierarchy.

## Shared principles
H-3DGS shares the fundamental rendering equation of 3DGS, where a scene is represented as a collection of anisotropic 3D Gaussians. Each Gaussian $G_i$ is defined by a mean position $\mu_i$, a covariance matrix $\Sigma_i$ (parameterized by a rotation matrix $R_i$ and a scaling vector $s_i$), and view-dependent color coefficients represented by [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) (SH). The rendering process projects these 3D Gaussians to 2D ellipses on the image plane using a linearized projection matrix $J$ and a camera projection matrix $P$, resulting in a 2D covariance $\Sigma'$ and mean $\mu'$ [S1, unofficial]. The color $C$ at a pixel is computed via alpha [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) of the splatted Gaussians sorted by depth.

The core innovation of H-3DGS is the **Hierarchical Split Point Tree (HSPT)**. This structure organizes the scene into a hierarchy of spatial partitions (chunks) and levels of detail. During training, the scene is divided into chunks. Each chunk is trained independently to manage memory constraints. After training, the chunks are merged into a global hierarchy. The HSPT allows the renderer to select the appropriate level of detail based on the camera's distance to the Gaussians and the focal length, enabling efficient rendering of ultra-large scale environments by only loading necessary data from external memory [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### CityGaussian / VastGaussian / DoGaussian
These methods are siblings in the family of large-scale 3DGS optimizations. CityGaussian combines chunked training with per-chunk LoD selection using [LightGaussian](#8036-lightgaussian.md). [VastGaussian](#6000-vastgaussian.md) introduces decoupled appearance modeling and progressive partitioning. DoGaussian is another approach within this lineage. They are chosen when specific large-scale artifacts or appearance inconsistencies in chunked training need to be addressed beyond the basic hierarchy management of H-3DGS. See [CityGaussian / VastGaussian / DoGaussian](6143-citygaussian-vastgaussian-dogaussian.md).

### Octree-GS
[Octree-GS](#7341-octree-gs.md) uses an [octree structure](#2792-octree-based-structures.md) to manage Gaussian primitives, offering a different spatial partitioning strategy compared to the chunk-based HSPT of H-3DGS. It is chosen when a more regular, grid-based spatial hierarchy is preferred over the arbitrary chunk boundaries of H-3DGS. See [Octree-GS](7341-octree-gs.md).

### LightGaussian
LightGaussian focuses on compressing the [Gaussian representation](#5918-gaussian-based-representation.md) by pruning insignificant Gaussians and quantizing parameters. It is often used in conjunction with chunked training (e.g., in CityGaussian) to reduce memory footprint. It is chosen when the primary bottleneck is the storage size of the Gaussian attributes rather than the spatial hierarchy itself. See [LightGaussian](8036-lightgaussian.md).

### Scale-Adaptive Gaussian Splatting
This method adapts the scale of Gaussians dynamically during training to better fit the scene geometry. It differs from H-3DGS by focusing on the geometric fidelity of individual primitives rather than the hierarchical organization of chunks. It is chosen when high-frequency geometric details are critical. See [Scale-Adaptive Gaussian Splatting](8085-scale-adaptive-gaussian-splatting.md).

### Multi-scale filtering
[Multi-scale filtering](#8244-multi-scale-filtering.md) applies filtering operations at different scales to smooth or enhance the Gaussian representation. It is a post-processing or training regularization technique. It is chosen when noise or artifacts in the reconstructed surface need to be reduced. See [Multi-scale filtering](8244-multi-scale-filtering.md).

### Virtual Memory for 3D Gaussian Splatting
This approach manages memory by swapping Gaussian data between VRAM and system RAM. It is chosen when the scene size exceeds available VRAM but system RAM is abundant. It complements H-3DGS's chunking by handling the data transfer logic. See [Virtual Memory for 3D Gaussian Splatting](8403-virtual-memory-for-3d-gaussian-splatting.md).

### Gaussian clustering and merging
This technique groups similar Gaussians to reduce the total count. It is chosen when the goal is to reduce the number of primitives for faster rendering or lower storage. See [Gaussian clustering and merging](8436-gaussian-clustering-and-merging.md).

### Iterative Gaussian Synopsis
This method creates a simplified synopsis of the [Gaussian set](#2074-gaussianset-data-structure.md) iteratively. It is chosen for applications requiring real-time preview or low-bandwidth transmission. See [Iterative Gaussian Synopsis](9289-iterative-gaussian-synopsis.md).

### Budgeted Gaussian Splatting
This approach optimizes the Gaussian set under a strict memory or rendering budget. It is chosen when computational resources are severely constrained. See [Budgeted Gaussian Splatting](9672-budgeted-gaussian-splatting.md).

### Sequential Point Trees (SPTs)
[SPTs](#10290-sequential-point-trees-spts.md) are the underlying spatial data structure used in H-3DGS to manage the hierarchy. They define the split points and levels of detail. See [Sequential Point Trees (SPTs)](10290-sequential-point-trees-spts.md).

## Background
H-3DGS was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2024 as an extension of the original 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) method [S1, unofficial]. The [original 3DGS](#2805-3d-gaussian-splatting-rendering-software.md) method, proposed by Kerbl et al. in 2023, demonstrated high-quality real-time rendering but suffered from high memory consumption, making it unsuitable for large-scale scenes [S1, unofficial]. Prior methods for large-scale environments, such as those by Tancik et al. [2022] and Xu et al. [2023], employed [scene partitioning](#9444-scene-representation-and-partitioning.md) or multi-GPU strategies. H-3DGS specifically addresses the limitations of [chunk-based training](#3168-chunk-based-training.md), such as view-chunk misalignment, chunk bleeding, and chunk ghosting, by introducing a global LoD hierarchy [S1, unofficial]. The method is implemented in PyTorch and C++/[CUDA](#3671-dual-contouring-2d-cuda.md), utilizing the densification implementation of Kheradmand et al. [2024] [S1, unofficial]. It is used for ultra-large scale reconstruction, including aerial and street-level datasets.

## Sources
[S1] A LoD of Gaussians: Unified Training and Rendering for Ultra-Large Scale Reconstruction with External Memory, https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2507.01110, fetched 2026-10-28 (unofficial)
